input.reasoning_summary: All three challenges were refuted by the evidence. H1 challenged whether there was a larger driver than commodity costs. Evidence E2 shows that commodity costs (140 bps) was tied as the largest single contributor with product and packaging investments (140 bps), making it clearly one of the main drivers. H2 challenged whether commodity costs were actually favorable - this is directly refuted by E2 which explicitly states "140 basis points of higher commodity costs" as a negative factor. H3 challenged whether gross margin actually increased - this is refuted by E2 and E13 which confirm the gross margin decreased. The evidence review confirms that E2, E4, and E8 all ENTAIL the claim for the exact period (quarter ended September 30, 2026) and are HISTORICAL_FACT statements. The claim is fully supported: gross margin did decline in Q1 FY2027 (quarter ended September 30, 2026), and higher commodity costs were indeed one of the main drivers, contributing 140 basis points out of 350 total basis points of negative impacts before offsets.
